newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli soldier opens fire in Hebron, wounds eight.
newsitem.headline: Israeli soldier opens fire in Hebron, wounds eight.

text.p: An Israeli soldier opened fire in a crowded Hebron market on Wednesday, wounding eight Palestinians just as negotiators were closing in on a deal to hand over most of the town to self-rule.

Witnesses said the soldier emptied an entire magazine of his M-16 before soldiers arrested him and seized the gun. Security sources identified the gunman as Jewish settler Noam Friedman from Maale Adumim near Jerusalem.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned the shooting in a call to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and vowed to implement their peace deals, an aide to Arafat said.

"Mr Netanyahu said this will not prevent him from pursuing the peace process and implementing the deals," Abu Rdainah told Reuters, adding that negotiations scheduled for noon were delayed but not suspended.
It was not immediately clear why the soldier opened fire but Israel Radio, reporting on the investigation by security forces, said he did it try to sabotage the handover.

"There are eight wounded. One was in critical condition and was sent to Hadassah hospital (in Jerusalem). We thought he died but he didn't. He is in bad condition," Jibril Rajoub, chief of Palestinian security in the West Bank, told Reuters.

Witnesses said the attacker was a young man who wore an army uniform and on his head the skullcap of a religious Jew. The army said the soldier was not posted to Hebron, but went on his own to the town, a flashpoint of Arab-Israeli violence.
Abdul-Karim al-Atrash, a vegetable vendor, told Voice of Palestine radio there was no stone-throwing by Palestinians which might have triggered the shooting.
"I was sitting in the market and all of a sudden there was automatic firing. I fell on the ground, but the shooting continued. I was shot in the leg," he said.
Israeli Major-General Gabi Ofir, in charge of the West Bank, said troops were trying to restore calm in the town. Palestinian police were asked to help.

"This incident is very serious, simply very serious," Ofir told army radio. "A soldier dressed in uniform with a long M-16 opened fire at Arab residents in Gross Square which is next to the Jewish enclave of Avraham Avinu."
Netanyahu said earlier on Wednesday he and Arafat had yet to fix a summit to sew up a deal giving self-rule to Hebron. Some 400 Jews live in the heart of the town, home to 100,000 Arabs.

Three years ago a Jew from nearby Kiryat Arba settlement, dressed in an Israeli army uniform, massacred 29 Palestinian worshippers in the tomb of the biblical patriarchs before survivors beat him to death.
Security concerns and other issues have delayed the handover of most of Hebron to the Palestinians.

Jewish settlers in the town had said they were praying for a miracle to prevent Israeli troops from pulling back and warned of impending bloodshed. They scuffled with Palestinians on Tuesday and tried to take over Arab houses in the casbah.
"I appeal even at this moment to the prime minister: Don't sign an agreement that will endanger our lives," Hebron leader Rabbi Moshe Levinger told Israel Radio before the shooting.

But chief Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat told army radio after the shooting: "We have always been arguing with the Israeli government, and the previous government actually, that the real threat to peace is not the Palestinians.
"It's these settlers, these Israeli settlers," he said.
Jewish settlers, who number 130,000 in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, helped Netanyahu sweep to power in elections last May on a promise to be tough with the Palestinians.
But Netanyahu has come under pressure from Washington, Israel's closest ally, to honour peace deals and withdraw from Hebron, the last of seven West Bank towns due for self-rule.
Hebron settlers' spokesman Noam Arnon told Reuters the shooting pointed to the need for Israel to retain total control.
He said that if Palestinian police had been deployed, there could have been clashes between the PLO and Israelis after such an incident.
